_comment: Executed behaviour probes. Each runs a scenario of build/fixtures/probe-crate against the
pinned crates and records what the span stream actually contained.
The `control` field is what makes a probe evidence rather than a coincidence. A capture
that contains a string proves only that something produced it; it cannot distinguish 'the
option did this' from 'this was there anyway'. So a probe carries a second scenario,
identical but for the thing under test, whose expectation must come out the other way.
Both halves must hold or the verdict is `divergent`, which fails verify.py -- never a pass.
expect / control_expect: substring | absent:X | re:PATTERN | exit:N
B001 is not a span probe. It is a tripwire on this repository's central claim: that no
published artifact carries the option builders. If a future release re-exports them the
claim becomes vacuous, and a repository that went on asserting it would be worse than one

probes.question: Does the hosted document carry NO item named add_custom_field while the private capture does?
probes.note: A tripwire on this repository's central claim, not a span observation. The first draft of this probe searched the documents as text and came out `refuted` -- correctly, and that refutation is the finding in B002. Rewritten to ask the structured index whether any ITEM carries the name, which is the thing that decides whether a reader can look the method up.

probes.question: Does the hosted document SHOW add_custom_field being called while documenting no such method?
probes.note: The sharpest statement of why this repository exists. The crate's front-page documentation -- the first thing anyone reads -- chains six builder methods, and docs.rs documents none of them: the page for the type they are called on answers 404. A reader sees the call, searches for the method, finds nothing, and concludes they have misread the example. Found by accident: the first draft of B001 searched raw text, expected the name to be absent, and was refuted by this.

probes.question: Does registering the rule produce a node span at all?
probes.note: The control is the point: without the rule the same query under the same subscriber emits no node spans, so the span is the rule's doing and not the subscriber's.

probes.question: Does preview_limit(0) suppress datafusion.preview?
probes.note: preview_limit defaults to 0, so the absent case is also the default case. Worth knowing that setting preview_fn alone changes nothing.

probes.question: Does record_metrics(false) suppress the datafusion.metrics.* fields?
probes.note: record_metrics is off by default, which is the single most common reason a trace looks empty of numbers.

probes.question: Does add_custom_field reach a span only when the macro also declares the key?
probes.note: The sharpest probe here. Both halves call add_custom_field("env", "probe") with identical options; the only difference is whether the macro declares `env = field::Empty`. A tracing span's field set is fixed at creation, so the undeclared value goes nowhere -- silently, with no error at compile time or run time. Upstream's own comment in integration-utils says the same: custom fields keys must be defined at compile time.

probes.question: Does pretty_format_compact_batch draw the |===| header rule?
probes.note: The compact formatter's header separator is what distinguishes its output from pretty_format_batches at a glance, and no signature carries it.

probes.question: Do the node spans carry the CALLING crate's target rather than datafusion_tracing?
probes.note: The macros default target: to module_path!(), which expands at the call site. An EnvFilter written as datafusion_tracing=info therefore receives nothing at all. Both halves are the same capture read two ways, so this is recorded rather than confirmed -- there is no second construction that would come out the other way without passing target: explicitly.

probes.question: Does full() emit Rule spans that phase_only() does not?
probes.note: On a large plan the per-rule spans are the bulk of the trace volume, so this is the switch to reach for before sampling.

probes.question: Can the undocumented builder instrument the physical optimizer alone?
probes.note: There is no documented way to do this: full() and phase_only() are the whole published surface, and physical_optimizer() is on the builder that docs.rs answers 404 for. Both captures contain Phase spans, so the finding is that they differ -- which is why this probe uses the differs mode rather than an opposite.

probes.question: Does an INFO filter drop instrumentation emitted at DEBUG entirely?
probes.note: Choosing instrument_with_debug_spans! and then filtering at INFO produces a silent nothing. The two halves differ only in which macro built the rule.

probes.question: Does the DEBUG-level macro emit at DEBUG when nothing filters it?
probes.note: The level is baked into the macro's name, which is the only thing distinguishing the six of them and is invisible in a signature because there is no signature.
